questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Actually all four

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. Of course, there were some things that required a bit of extra time to figure out and get sorted out, but overall it went well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had two information days very early on in the process, where we were introduced to the most important information. This was a great help and gave the feeling that the university took good care of its exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I already knew quite a few Norwegians from Bergen beforehand, so in my case I found a room in the city centre through mutual friends. However, I believe it would have been significantly more difficult if one did not have the same network as I did.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive and can be difficult to find

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had an information meeting on the first day, where we received guidance on how to register and obtain our student cards, which were necessary for access to the campus, exams, and so on

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information at campus and on e-mail

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes that I wanted even though I wanted an "atypical course" for exchange students because I wanted a course in Norwegian so I found it very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask if you have any questions and don't be afraid to reach out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two master’s-level courses – one taught in English and one in Norwegian. I found the teaching to be most successful in my Norwegian course (intellectual property law), as the lecturers were extremely competent and the course was well structured and well organised. The English-taught course was also fine, but I generally experienced a lack of clear information throughout the course, and the teaching did not go particularly deep into the syllabus. That being said, it was not a bad course; however, I found that the academic level of the teaching staff was highest in my Norwegian course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a considerable amount of group work, presentations, and lectures, which closely corresponds to the teaching methods I am familiar with from the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Human Rights and Welfare Policies - Master (10 ECTS)
Immaterialrett (20 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Immaterialrett (20 ECTS) to other danish students who wants to go on exchange to Norway. It was a very good course and having a course in norwegian really helped me to understand the norwegian language.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The costs of books, fitness, and food were higher than I had expected. Norway is an expensive country to live in as a young student without a job

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, books, fitness

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many different student associations, where you could engage in activities ranging from sports to playing chess. In addition, there were various events for exchange students, such as walks, game nights, and similar activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Walks and Friday bars. They were pleasant opportunities to meet new people and feel like part of the community.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hikes, trips outside of the town

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Norwegians and Danes are very similar

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No just be yourself

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendliness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: An exchange is not always easy. You will be challenged and find yourself in unfamiliar situations that you have to handle on your own, but once you get through them, you will be very proud of yourself. In addition, I would say that it is a great opportunity for personal development – both socially and academically.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting many new people, learning how to study at a new university, and independently finding all the necessary information were very rewarding experiences. However, my greatest personal achievement was giving a presentation entirely on my own in English to my English-taught course, as well as taking an oral exam in Norwegian and receiving a grade of 10 (B), which was a very significant achievement for me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing friends and family

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
